items.method: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) equipped with energy dispersive X-ray analysis (EDX)
items.quote: The samples, which were characterized as two-phase by XRD, were further examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) equipped with energy dispersive X-ray analysis (EDX).

The enthalpy of formation for HfGe2 was measured using the Kleppa-type High Temperature Reaction Calorimeter (HTRC) [21] with the calorimeter temperature set at 1100 ± 2 °C. The experiment was carried out under the protection of argon gas.

Drop Calorimetry method was used to measure the heat contents for the HfGe2 and Hf3Ge. The measurements from 400 to 1050 °C at intervals of 100 °C were carried out in an argon atmosphere using a high temperature calorimeter.
The annealed alloys were firstly subjected to the XRD powder measurement.
Six samples, each with a weight of about 100 mg, were produced by mixing elemental powders of Ge and Hf in a mortar according to the molar ratio of HfGe2 phase, and pressing them into small pellets.
